html:
Picture this: a conference table stacked with $2,000 worth of corporate gifts: engraved pens, branded leather notebooks and monogrammed wine glasses. Six months later, many of those gifts may be sitting in a drawer, heading to a charity bin or ending up in recycling.

Now picture an alternative: a tailored suit, two custom dress shirts and a pair of hand-finished shoes. Three years later, the recipient may still wear them to board meetings, client presentations and important events. That is the difference between a corporate gift and a corporate statement.

For HR directors, executive assistants and founders in Bangkok and across Southeast Asia, bespoke corporate gifting offers something more personal than standard branded merchandise. It is wearable, useful and made around the individual receiving it.

Why Does Bespoke Tailoring Outperform Traditional Corporate Gifts?

Traditional corporate gifts often have three common problems:

  • Low utility: A branded power bank may sit unused in a drawer.

  • Low recall: An engraved paperweight or logo tote bag is easy to forget after the initial presentation.

  • Limited emotional value: Generic merchandise rarely feels personal to the person receiving it.

Bespoke corporate gifts, including a fitted suit, custom shirts or hand-finished shoes, offer a different kind of value. They are designed to be worn regularly, remembered for years and connected to a personal fitting experience that generic merchandise cannot replicate.

A tailored garment also avoids the one-size-fits-all approach of standard gifting. The recipient chooses fabrics, details and styling preferences, making the gift feel considered rather than transactional.

What Is the Difference Between Bespoke Corporate Gifts and Branded Merchandise?

Bespoke corporate gifts are personal, fitted and built for long-term use. A tailored suit, custom shirt or pair of shoes is made around the recipient’s measurements and style preferences.

Branded merchandise is generally generic, logo-led and designed for broad distribution. While it can be useful for events or promotions, it rarely creates the same sense of recognition as a garment made specifically for the person receiving it.

How Can Custom Tailoring Build Brand Identity Across a Team?

A team that looks unified often appears more confident and prepared. Custom tailoring allows companies to align fabric, fit and styling across an entire department, regional office or leadership team without creating the stiff uniformity of rental tuxedos or logo-heavy workwear.

The result is a wardrobe that communicates intention rather than company swag.

Companies can coordinate colours, shirt styles, accessories or jacket fabrics while allowing each person to retain their own fit and preferences. This creates a polished team look without making every employee wear an identical outfit.

What Corporate Gifting Packages Are Available?

Forward-thinking companies do not choose one gift and hope it works. They match the gift to the occasion.

The Executive Tier is designed for C-suite recognition, founder-to-investor gifting, board member appreciation and major client thank-yous. At $800–$1,500 per person, it includes one bespoke suit, two custom dress shirts and a pair of hand-finished leather shoes.

The Professional Tier is suited to senior hires, promotion celebrations, mid-tier client gifting and five- or ten-year tenure awards. Priced at $400–$700 per person, it includes three custom shirts, a tailored blazer and curated accessories such as ties, pocket squares or cufflinks.

The Team Tier is designed for department-wide gifts, team-building events and conferences. At $300–$500 per person, it includes coordinated shirts, accessories and an optional on-site or in-shop styling session with a professional photographer for team headshots.

The Welcome Aboard Tier works well for new hires, interns and probation-period completion gifts. At $200–$400 per person, it includes two starter shirts and a personal style consultation. It sets the tone from day one: we invest in our people.

How Much Should a Corporate Gift Cost Per Person?

Corporate gifting budgets can range from $200 to $1,500 per person, depending on the recipient, the occasion and the level of personalisation required.

Executive recognition gifts may sit within the $800–$1,500 range, while professional milestone gifts can fall between $400–$700. Team and onboarding gifts commonly sit between $200–$500 per person.

Bespoke packages combine a practical garment with a personal fitting and styling experience, giving the recipient something they can use long after the initial presentation.

How Can Companies Use Bespoke Corporate Gifts?

Bespoke corporate gifting can support onboarding, employee recognition, client relationships and milestone celebrations.

A growing technology company may use the Welcome Aboard Tier for a new engineering hire class. Instead of standard welcome boxes, each new hire can receive two custom shirts in colours that complement the company’s visual identity, alongside a short style consultation. The shirts then become useful wardrobe pieces for client meetings, presentations and company events.

A law firm recognising partners who reach a five-year milestone may choose the Professional Tier. Three custom shirts, a tailored blazer and accessories provide a more substantial gift than a standard voucher while remaining appropriate for a professional setting. A private fitting at the atelier also gives the recipient an experience that feels personal.

A founder looking to thank key early customers may choose the Executive Tier. A tailored suit, two shirts and shoes create a more thoughtful gesture than branded merchandise, particularly when the founder attends the fitting or presents the gift personally.

Are Bespoke Suits Good Corporate Gifts?

Yes. Bespoke suits can make excellent corporate gifts because they are personal, practical and built around the recipient’s individual requirements.

Unlike generic merchandise, a tailored suit can be worn repeatedly for meetings, events, presentations and formal occasions. The fitting process also gives the recipient time to choose fabrics, styling details and finishing touches that reflect their personal taste.

What Does the Bespoke Corporate Experience Include?

A corporate gifting programme is more than a bulk order. The fitting experience itself can become an important brand touchpoint, particularly for onboarding, leadership recognition and client hospitality.

A corporate tailoring experience can include:

  • Individual measurements and fitting guidance

  • Fabric, shirt, suit and accessory selection

  • Personal styling advice based on the recipient’s role and preferences

  • Alterations and final fitting appointments

  • Batch delivery for larger teams

  • Digital measurement storage for future re-orders

Jesse & Son can arrange a master tailor and fitter to visit an office for a half-day or full-day fitting session. Teams can be measured, fitted and styled in one organised event, while the session can also become a team-building moment.

For executive tiers and key client programmes, Jesse & Son’s Bangkok atelier can host private fitting days with dedicated fitting rooms and personalised styling advice.

How Do Pricing, Logistics and International Shipping Work?

Bespoke corporate gifting programmes require more planning than off-the-rack orders. Clear timelines, measurements and delivery logistics help create a smooth experience for both the company and its recipients.

Team bookings of 10 or more may receive 10–15% off per-person pricing, while larger corporate accounts can benefit from dedicated account management and priority scheduling. Quotes can be itemised by tier and recipient, helping HR and finance teams plan by department, milestone or event.

A standard bespoke order generally runs 4–6 weeks from measurement to delivery, depending on the garment requirements, fitting schedule and production workload. On-site fitting days can be scheduled with as little as two weeks of lead time depending on team size. Rush production may be available for an additional fee, although most corporate programmes benefit from planning ahead.

Jesse & Son also ships finished garments worldwide, with completed measurements stored digitally for future re-orders. For companies with teams across Asia, Europe and North America, this can help maintain consistency when ordering garments for new hires, replacement pieces or future corporate events.

What Should You Look for in a Corporate Gifting Partner?

Not every tailor is set up to manage a corporate programme. Before committing, consider the tailor’s experience, production process, measurement storage and consultation support.

A tailor who can dress one executive is not automatically equipped to manage fittings for forty new hires. Corporate programmes require different logistics, staffing and scheduling, particularly when garments need to be delivered at the same standard and within the same timeframe.

In-house production can also support consistency across a corporate account. It helps with quality control, fabric selection and coordination when companies need garments that feel aligned without appearing identical.

Digital measurement storage matters because a corporate programme should not end with the first delivery. Stored measurements and fabric preferences can make future orders for new hires, replacement garments or repeat corporate events more efficient.

Why Should Companies Gift Something Recipients Will Actually Wear?

The next time your company budgets for recognition, onboarding or client gifting, ask one question: will the recipient still be using this in three years?

Bespoke corporate gifting, including suits, shirts and shoes made for the recipient, is designed to meet that test. It works because it is personal, practical and connected to an experience where the recipient is measured, fitted and styled as an individual.

Frequently Asked Questions

How Do You Tailor for a Whole Team?

To tailor for a whole team, schedule a corporate fitting day either on-site, where a tailor visits your office, or at the tailor’s atelier, where the team attends in groups.

Each person is measured, chooses fabrics and receives individual styling guidance. Production then runs according to the agreed timeline, with finished garments delivered in batches where required.

What Is a Corporate Tailoring Experience?

A corporate tailoring experience is a structured programme where a tailor measures, fits and styles multiple employees or clients, either at the company’s office or at the tailor’s atelier.

It can include fabric selection, measurement, fitting, alterations and final delivery. Companies often use this type of experience for onboarding, employee recognition and team-building events.

What Are Good Corporate Gifts for Executives?

Good corporate gifts for executives include bespoke tailored suits, custom dress shirts, hand-finished leather shoes, premium watches, fine writing instruments and curated experiences such as private dining or travel.

Wearable bespoke gifts are particularly effective because they are useful, personal and designed for repeated use.

Can Corporate Garments Be Reordered Later?

Yes. Once measurements and preferences are stored, companies can place future orders for new hires, replacement garments or additional pieces more easily.

This can be useful for growing teams, repeat recognition programmes and companies managing wardrobe consistency across multiple locations.
